scope: Proposition 8.2 (Projected screening) of the manuscript “Pure-Point Spectrum for the Two-Dimensional Anderson Model at Every Positive Disorder” (preprints/Pure-Point-Spectrum-for-the-Two-Dimensional-Anderson-Model-at-Every-Positive-Disorder-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 261 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 17487e3a2720b36f), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 49. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: For all the systems just described, Π⊤ GΠ ≤ Cn. (8.7) Give cost one to nearest-neighbor edges whose endpoints both belong to counted good cores, and cost zero to other edges; any of the positive costs may also be dropped. If two source and response sectors of Π have cost distance at least t, their resolvent block has norm at most Cn exp(−cnt). Suppose, further, that two systems agree on an inner region and a surrounding shield, including all ports there, and that counted good tests in the shield are usable in both systems. Count costs only on shared good-good edges in the shield. If every crossing of the shield from the inner region to the exterior costs at least t, then the responses between common inner ports differ by at most Cn exp(−cnt) in operator norm. This includes comparison with a Dirichlet restriction buffered beyond the shield.
